rows.heading: ## Mutation-sweep recipe — numbered steps; bounded cold-read evidence
rows.claim: Bash grammar: `bad-case 05 undeclared-file want exit=1 token=SURFACE UNLISTED got exit=0` and summary `SELFTEST: FAIL (1/16 cases)`
rows.excerpt:
- B1 (1): `bad-case 05 undeclared-file want exit=1 token=SURFACE UNLISTED got exit=0`. The guard
  inversion makes `verify_unlisted` return early whenever scan dirs **exist** (`:241-242`), so the
  UNLISTED arm goes quiet; the clean case still passes because its fixture has no stray child to
  miss — the single case that pins the arm is the one that fires.
rows.note: The bad-case exemplar is verbatim at corpus/knowledge/mutation-case-kagi-census.md:84 ('bad-case 05 undeclared-file want exit=1 token=SURFACE UNLISTED got exit=0'). The summary quote is not: `SELFTEST: FAIL (1/16 cases)` occurs nowhere in the pointed range, and nowhere in the file - `git -C LANE grep -n 'SELFTEST: FAIL' BASE -- corpus/knowledge/mutation-case-kagi-census.md` prints nothing (the only `SELFTEST: FAIL` hits in the lane at BASE are under .ufo/evidence/kaika-round-1/coldread/, e.g. appendixB/B1.out:38). What the note actually records is the failing suite line in the kill-rate table at :67, as `1/16` / FAIL, and that line is outside the cited :82-103. So the target supports the grammar exemplar but not the quoted summary - half the clause is unsourced at the pointed place: stale, not a drift of line numbers. The minimal repair keeps the pointer count at one: extend the range to :67 and quote the note's own recorded form (see proposed_fix). Shown by: git -C LANE show BASE:corpus/knowledge/mutation-case-kagi-census.md | sed -n '67p;82,103p' and the git grep above.

rows.heading: ## Mutation-sweep recipe — numbered steps; bounded cold-read evidence
rows.claim: **A kill can be token-only, not exit-only.** B4's deleted symlink arm kept the exit code (the row fell into the regular-file arm, `got exit=1` like the expected one) and died on the token assert alone
rows.excerpt:
- B4 (1): `bad-case 07 symlink-swap want exit=1 token=SURFACE LINK got exit=1` — the **exit code
  still matched** (the deleted arm's symlink falls into the regular-file arm and prints
  `SURFACE DIVERGED`); the token assert is what killed it.
rows.note: corpus/knowledge/mutation-case-kagi-census.md:88-91 is exactly the cited incident: '`bad-case 07 symlink-swap want exit=1 token=SURFACE LINK got exit=1` - the **exit code still matched** (the deleted arm's symlink falls into the regular-file arm and prints `SURFACE DIVERGED`); the token assert is what killed it.' That is the clause's 'kept the exit code ... the row fell into the regular-file arm, got exit=1 like the expected one ... died on the token assert alone'. Direct support; no drift. Shown by: git -C LANE show BASE:corpus/knowledge/mutation-case-kagi-census.md | sed -n '88,91p'.
